Commentary.Commentary: Right then! A win each for all three teams in the two legs of the Tri-series so far. The carnival now moves to Barbados with South Africa taking on Australia on the 19th of this month. The Proteas are on top and whoever wins that game will make it through to the final. Who will be that winner? Do join us on Sunday, 19th June, 2016 at 2230 IST (1700 GMT) for all the action. Until then, Adios! Take care!

IMRAN TAHIR has been named the MAN OF THE MATCH for his 7-fer. Humbly says that it was his wife who reminded him this morning that he was two wickets away from 100 scalps and credits Shamsi's bowling partnership with him for turning the game around. Confidently says that there was never a doubt that South Africa would play the way they did tonight and all would be very happy. Is proud of the way Shamsi has grown as a cricketer and says that he is like a younger brother. Does not have much idea about the pitch at Barbados and says that he has heard it does not have much for the spinners but is looking forward to the challenge.

Victorious SA skipper AB de Villiers says that the Proteas have a lot of talent in the batting order and credits this as a much better performance than the previous 3 games. States that there was always the belief that they could win all games and that is what resulted in a win tonight. Praises Tahir and also Shamsi for their performances. Adds that with 10 points, just one of their remaining 2 games needs to be won but they will try and win both games and focus on their contest against Australia on the 19th in Barbados.

West Indies captain, JASON HOLDER is disappointed with the way his side bowled in the first 10 overs. Is adamant that his decision to bowl first was correct, just that they did not execute their plans well. Hopes to come back hard in the last leg and go through to the final and also hopes for a good turnout in the crowd.

The Proteas did not have a great start with the ball but then came back well in the middle overs. Tahir showed why he is considered a world-class spinner as he picked up a record 7-wicket haul while Shamsi did well with a couple of scalps.
Pollard and Holder tried some resurrection but it was too much to ask of them. Eventually, the home side folded up for 204.

It was a pitch which took some turn and was a bit slow. Fletcher and Charles made full use of Powerplay 1 but then after the spinners were introduced, the hosts lost their way. From 69/0, they were reduced to 128/5 and did not recover.

2 massive wins, 2 bonus points and South Africa are on top of the points table. What a clinical overall display. Excellent batting to rack up 343 and then Tahir ran through the Windies to demolish them.
